solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Very rapid form of percussion

indicators.note: a form of something is a version of it, so the letters of the next word are given a new shape

explanation.surface: A drummer's style of playing is said to be extremely fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' tells you to rearrange PERCUSSION; 'Very rapid' looks like praise for a drum style but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something supersonic travels faster than sound, which makes it extremely fast.

clue.text: One upper-class twit

parts.note: U is a classic label for upper-class usage
a nit is a fool, a twit

explanation.surface: A remark on a single aristocratic fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single whole thing, a quantity of one.

clue.text: It may hold what has to be laid on the table

definitions.text: It may hold what has to be laid on the table

parts.words: It may hold what has to be laid on the table
parts.note: seems to be about a document to be tabled at a meeting, but means a breakfast item that holds something laid by a hen

explanation.surface: A folder carrying a proposal that must be tabled at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A small breakfast cup holds a boiled egg, which a hen has laid, on the table.

clue.text: Trying to interview royalty?

parts.note: to see someone is to meet or interview them
a king is royalty

explanation.surface: A journalist attempts to get an audience with a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeking means trying or attempting to obtain something, as in seeking a job.

clue.text: Corner disallowed

parts.note: reading the answer as NO plus OK gives not okay, which means disallowed

explanation.surface: A referee rules a corner kick out of order.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer split in two gives a phrase meaning the clue's last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a small sheltered corner or recess in a room.

clue.text: Understand and win popularity

definitions.meaning: to grasp the meaning of something

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb can mean grasping an idea or becoming fashionable.

clue.text: Another chess victory for ship's officer

parts.note: a second one is another
mate, short for checkmate, wins a chess game

explanation.surface: A ship's officer wins a second game of chess.
explanation.definitionFit: The second mate is a merchant ship's officer ranking below the first mate.

clue.text: Tender after getting the stick? One may treat you

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece comes after, below, the first

parts.note: a staff is a walking stick
to tend or nurse the sick

explanation.surface: After a beating with a stick, someone tender needs treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' is not the adjective but the verb sense, someone who tends.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff nurse is a qualified hospital nurse who treats patients.

clue.text: Exploit a twist of fate

indicators.note: twisting the word fate jumbles its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone takes advantage of an unexpected turn of fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exploit' reads as a verb, but here it is the noun meaning a bold deed.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploit, used as a noun, is a daring achievement, an impressive deed.

clue.text: Chose to give voice — escorted from the scene

parts.note: to give voice in song is to sing
someone escorted away has been led out

explanation.surface: A performer decided to sing and was then shown off the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To single out someone is to pick them in particular, so the phrase is a synonym of chose.

clue.text: Intercept and separate

definitions.meaning: to stop something on its way, as a message or a supply line is stopped
isolated, apart from others, as a village in snow

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase can mean blocking something on its route or, as an adjective, being isolated from others.

clue.text: Hang having to pay to take us in!

indicators.note: together with the later word in, this says one piece takes another inside it
completes the phrase take ... in, meaning hold the second piece within the first

parts.note: to spend money is to pay it out
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint about being left dangling while being made to foot the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark mimics an indignant taxpayer; 'to take ... in' is one split indicator, the container's two halves either side of the inserted word.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend something is to hang it from above, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Same agents, but different actors adopt them

indicators.note: the letters are made different by being rearranged

explanation.surface: The same agents, but the performers they represent call themselves otherwise.
explanation.definitionFit: Performers often use professional names, chosen pseudonyms, instead of their real ones.

clue.text: Article has wrong emphasis about ocean-going craft

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other
putting the letters wrong rearranges them

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece lays undue stress on sea-going vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' suggests a boat, but here it means skill. 'wrong' gives SEAMSHIP, and 'about' wraps it round the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Seamanship is the skill of handling a ship on the open sea.

clue.text: Criticise when I left dry ice swirling around

indicators.note: the letter I departs from the mixed letters
swirling stirs the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint about dry ice on stage swirling about once a performer has left.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I from DRY ICE and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To decry is to publicly denounce or condemn something.

clue.text: Composer born, I do recall, in the 1830s

indicators.note: read as re-call, calling the words up again in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone recollects that a certain composer was born in the 1830s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recall' rearranges BORN plus I DO; 'in the 1830s' is a true aside, since the Russian composer was born in 1833.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Borodin was a Russian composer, writer of the opera Prince Igor.

clue.text: Go up in public transport intended to take in others

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a bus is public transport

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading from the bottom, backwards

explanation.surface: Someone boards a bus meant to carry other passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take in' looks like giving a lift but means deceive.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bogus is fake, designed to deceive or take people in.

clue.text: Board makes progress

definitions.meaning: to board a bus or train is to climb aboard it
to advance or do well, as someone getting along in a career

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both climbing aboard a vehicle and advancing or succeeding.

clue.text: A course taken abroad

parts.note: a course or route is a way

explanation.surface: Someone enrolls on a course of study taken in another country.
explanation.definitionFit: Being abroad means being in foreign parts, far from home, and so absent.

clue.text: Sunny with strong wind

parts.note: f, for forte, is the musical abbreviation for loud or strong
a wind is a moving current of air

explanation.surface: A weather forecast promising bright skies and a gale.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair weather is bright and dry, so it describes a sunny day.

clue.text: Trouble with the throat or back of a horse

definitions.meaning: an inflammation of the windpipe in children, with a barking cough
the rump or hindquarters of a horse

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a childhood throat infection and the rump of a horse.

clue.text: Under a hundred girls make up the school

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits under, below, another

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: Fewer than a hundred girls form the whole school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under a hundred' looks like a number but it places LASSES below C.
explanation.definitionFit: A school is made up of its classes, groups of pupils taught together.

clue.text: Trailblazer needs one in support

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar
taken as written

explanation.surface: An explorer requires someone to back them up.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is the first to explore or develop something, blazing a trail.

clue.text: As you say, it's precisely what's required

definitions.meaning: a reply agreeing fully with what someone has just said
fitting the need with complete accuracy

explanation.definitionFit: The adverb is both an emphatic word of agreement and a word meaning precisely or accurately.

clue.text: Sees trouble when I am taken in by a cat

indicators.note: one piece is held inside another
to trouble something is to disturb it, so the letters are stirred

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is upset on finding a cat has fooled them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' turns SEES into SESE, and 'taken in by' puts I AM after its first S.
explanation.definitionFit: A Siamese is a breed of cat, so the answer is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Smiled wryly when given the wrong directions

indicators.note: wryly suggests a twisted way, so the letters are twisted

explanation.surface: Someone smiled ruefully on being told the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: To be misled is to have been directed wrongly or deceived.

clue.text: Judge gives fools direction

parts.note: asses are foolish people
S, for south, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A judge tells the idiots where to go.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess is to evaluate or form a judgement about something, so the verbs agree.

clue.text: Female member of German union

parts.note: seems to be a trade unionist, but the union is a marriage in Germany, so the word is the German for wife

explanation.surface: A woman belonging to a German trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: The German for a married woman or wife, a partner in a marriage.

clue.text: Like to get first-class return for the continent

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons

indicators.note: a return goes back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: A1 is the label for first-class

explanation.surface: Someone wants a first-class return ticket to another continent.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 as AI is reversed to IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest of the world's continents.

clue.text: One breaking art's rules in bizarre fashion

definitions.text: One breaking art's rules in bizarre fashion

indicators.note: the letter breaks into the middle of the jumbled letters
the letters are arranged in a strange, rearranged way

parts.note: the word arts with its letter s
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Describes an artist who flouts the conventions of art in strange ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in bizarre fashion' rearranges ARTS RULES, and 'breaking' puts I into it; the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Surrealists such as Dali defied artistic conventions with dreamlike, strange imagery.

clue.text: Live up to a wicked description

indicators.note: in a down light up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

explanation.surface: Someone tries to match a reputation for being bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses LIVE in this across entry as well, a common convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil and wicked are close synonyms describing morally bad behaviour.

clue.text: With fair agreement, quits board

parts.note: when two people are quits they are square, owing nothing
deal is sawn pine or fir board

explanation.surface: Someone resigns from a company's board on reasonable terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quits' looks like a verb but is the adjective meaning even, and 'board' is timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A square deal is an honest bargain giving both sides just treatment.
